Diagnosis: The previous grounded output used both 'freeze_orientation' and 'axis_align' in the same constraint set, which the schema strictly disallows ('Mixes freeze_orientation with other orientation constraints (not allowed)'). Only one orientation operator is allowed per set. The correct one for this subtask is 'axis_align' because the intent is to keep the gripper's tool +z axis antiparallel to the handle -y axis throughout the approach, not to freeze the gripper orientation globally (which would risk misaligning the approach axis if orientation wasn't set properly beforehand).
Reasoning: Success for this subtask means: 1) the gripper must remain open while approaching (open_gripper); 2) the gripper's tool +z axis must remain antiparallel to the handle's -y axis (axis_align), establishing the approach direction and keeping orientation fixed in a relative sense to the object; 3) the gripper must move into contact with the center of the handle (reach_point), but the approach can also terminate early if high effort/contact is sensed (indicating contact has occurred). Only 'axis_align' is retained for orientation, as using 'freeze_orientation' together with it violates schema. 'open_gripper' is needed as the gripper must remain open. The positional goal uses a single 'reach_point', and a logic 'or' is used to allow the constraint to be satisfied by either reaching the intended position or by detecting high contact effort (both ways contact may be detected in practice), as per the subtask text.
